composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate required fields first, so a missing/blank field is a 400 listing every
# offending field before the body is mapped to an entity.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkTelephoneUnique

# Reject with 409 when the normalized telephone is already used by another owner.
checkTelephoneUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkHouseholdUnique

# Reject with 409 when another owner shares this last name and address (compared
# case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the body sets 'sharesHousehold' true.
checkHouseholdUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# When the body set 'sharesHousehold' true, assign the new owner and the existing
# same-lastName/same-address owner(s) a single stable, shared 'householdId'.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

# Record how many existing owners share this owner's firstName and lastName
# (case-insensitively), before it is saved so the count excludes it.
assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCode

# Assign the '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' customer code before saving, so the owner count the
# sequence is derived from excludes this not-yet-persisted owner.
assignCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

The change is complete and the full test suite is green (26 tests, 0 failures/errors).

## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` with a per-city sequence.

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** (the one place the code is built) now:
- Takes `CITY3` = upper-cased first three letters of the owner's city.
- Keeps `LAST3` = upper-cased first three letters of the last name.
- Computes `NNNN` as a **per-city** sequence — one more than the number of existing owners already in that city (counted case-insensitively over `findAll()`, before the new owner is saved so it's excluded), zero-padded to 4 digits.

**Values derived from `customerCode` rebuild automatically:** the `membershipNumber` in `OwnerMapper` is `<customerCode>-M<YY>`, so it now naturally reads e.g. `SYD-ALP-0001-M26` since it's composed from the (new) `customerCode` field rather than re-deriving from name — no code change needed there, only the doc-comment example updated.

I also updated the doc comments in `AssignCustomerCode.java`, the `owners.POST.yml` step comment, and the `OwnerMapper` example to reflect the new format.

Tests confirming the behavior: `Cp16` (format regex `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`), `Cp09` (same-city consecutive sequence, `SYD-ALP-`/`SYD-BRA-`), and `Cp14` (membership number over the city-prefixed code) all pass, along with the rest of the suite.
